0.1 This Indian Standard
Standards Institution Brushware Sectional Division Council.

FOREWORD

( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian on 30 April 1986, after the draft finalized by the Committee had been approved by the Chemical

0.2 Welder's brush forms an important part of welding accessories. With the rapid industrialization within the country, welding operations in fabrication work have constantly increased resulting in the increase in demand of welder's burshes. With this background the standard was first published in 1967 so that the production of standard size of welder's brushes could be achieved. 0.3 With the growth of engineering industry in the diverse field since this specification was formulated in 1967, the existing two sizes of this brush have been found inadequate now to meet the varied requirements from different sections of end-users. And as such the sizes of the brush have been increased from the existing two to five in this revision of the specification. 0.3.1 Also, practical difficulties are being experienced at the production stage of the brush to adhere to some of the details stipulated in the existing specification. Therefore, necessary modification in these details have been made in this revisions. 0.3.2 Attempt has also been made to render the specification in a more graphic form as far as possible, in places of descriptive clauses to make this revised version of the specification easily comprehensive so as to extend the scope of implementation of this standard to the village level of this industry which plays a vital role to feed the demand of this product from various sectors. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in 3

IS:4517

-1986

accordance with IS : 2-1960? The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and test for welder's brush. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, IS : 384-19791_ shall apply. 3. SIZES 3.1 The width at the brush-heads along with the numbers of rows of the tufts of the filling material shall denote the size of the brush and shall be as follows: a) 20 mm b) 25 mm c) 40 mm d) 50 mm e) 60 mm 4. REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Materials - Welder's following materials. brush shall be manufactured from the 2 rows of tufts, 3 rows of tufts, 4 rows of tufts, 5 rows of tufts, and 6 rows of tufts. the definitions given in 2 of and methods of sampling

4.1.1 Filling Material - This shall consist of hardened and tempered bright, blue or black round steel wire @30 to 0'355 mm in diameter or as agreed to between the manufacturer and the supplier. 4.1.1.1 Tuft of Filling Material - Each tuft shall comprise 16 to 18 numbers of wires ( 32 to 36 strands when folded ) on average or as agreed to between the manufacturer and supplier. 4.1.2 Drawing Wir+--Bright 0.60 mm in diameter. steel or galvanized iron wire 0.45 to

4.1.4 Staples-

Bright iron wire 0.9 to I.0 mm in diameter. A shall

4.1.5 Timber -Any of the timber species listed in Appendix be used in the manufacture of the wooden portion of the brush.

4.1.5.1 The timber shall be reasonably straight-grained and wellseasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent when tested by In case of dispute, the oven-dry method the electronic moisture meter. shall be used (see Appendix B ). 4.1.5.2 The timber shall be free from brashness, any kind of decay rot, insect attack, centre heart ( pith ), knots ( except pin knots ), cracks, warp and any other defects which may reduce the life of the brush or affect its utility. 4.2 Dimensions andTolerances

4.2.1 The brushes shall conform to the dimensions given in Fig. IA and lB, and Table 1.

4.9 Manufacture 4.5.1 The brushes shall generally conform to the shapes, designs and shall fulfil the details of requirements as illustrated in Fig. IA and lB, and Table 1. However, the distance of the first hole shall be 1Omm from the edge of the board.

4.3.2 Wire-drawn Brushes-The requisite numbers of tufts shall be drawn with the drawing wire inside the tuft hole and securely fastened at The wooden back/cover the back of the stock/board of the brush-heads. shall be placed suitably and shall be firmly nailed as shown in Fig. 1 for wire-drawn brushes. 4.3.2.1 Staple-set brushes - The requisite numbers of tufts shall be slogged with the staple into the tuft hole and shall be firmly anchored with the wooden stock/board. -No back/cover is required. 4.3.2.2 Trimming - The working straight-faced for both the wire-drawn Suitable 4.3.2.3 Preservation applied on the filling material. 4.4 Workmanship

MARKING 5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor or inspection authority and the supplier, each bursh shall be legibly and indelibly marked or stamped with the manufacturer's name or recognized trademark, if any, size, and the year of manufacture. 5.1.1 The brushes Certification Mark. may also $be suitably marked with the IS1

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the testing and requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that Details of conditions under which a licence for the standard as a further safeguard. use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

APPENDIX ( Clause 7.1 )
SAMPLING C-O. GENERAL OF BRUSH,

C

WELDER'S

C-O.1 The supplier shall submit three identical brushes for approval. C-O.2 The indentor or the inspection authority shall retain one of the three samples approved against each item till the completion of the order. C-l. SCALE OF SAMPLING

C-l.1 Lot - In any consignment, all the brushes of the same size and quality shall be divided into groups of 500 brushes or less and each such group shall constitute a lot. Care shall be taken to ensure that brushes included in a lot do not differ in construction, as far as possible. C-1.1.1 The conformity of the brushes in a lot to the requirements of this specification shall be ascertained for each lot separately. The number of brushes to be selected for this purpose shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2. C-1.1.2 The brushes shall randomness of the selection recommended for use: be selected at random. one of the following To ensure proceduresis

4

If all the brushes in a lot are packed in one box, then starting from any brush, count them in any suitable order as 1, 2, . . . . . . up to I and so on, where r is the integral part of N/n ( .Nand n being the lot size and sample size respectively ). Every rth brush thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. 11

IS s 4517 - 1986 b) If the brushes in a lot are packed in more than one box, approximately equal number of brushes shall be picked up at random from as many boxes -as possible so as to obtain the required number of brushes as specified in Table 2.
